name: Force Pad
description: A 1x1 m launch pad. Step on it and it throws the VR player UP and FORWARD on a ballistic arc — a force vector you trigger with your feet. Glowing plate with forward chevrons and a live launch-vector arrow (up + forward) showing exactly where you'll fly. Uses the proven jump_pad / XRToolsPlayerBody.velocity player-launch path. DNA: forward_force, up_force, cooldown_time.
theoreticalGrounding: A launch is just a velocity you're given. v0 = forward*forward_force + up*up_force; gravity does the rest. Impulse made bodily.

dna.default: foresight=none, vectors=velocity - together these are the shipped pad exactly: the glowing plate, the neon frame, the three chevrons and ONE cyan launch-vector arrow, with no arc drawn anywhere. All 8 existing placements are untouched. apply_grid_config no longer frees every child and re-runs _ready() on any call - it rebuilds only when a value actually changed and only after the first build.
dna.was: a launch pad whose only exports were magnitudes - forward_force, up_force, cooldown_time. Turning them made the same pad throw you further; none of them was an argument, and the launch itself is an event no still can hold.
dna.note: catapult's two words reused character for character: foresight = how much of the ARC is handed to you before you fire, vectors = how 'what you give' is drawn at the launch point. Same machine at two scales - both hand a body a velocity and let gravity have it back. Only the DEFAULT differs, and it differs honestly: the catapult was born showing its whole parabola, the pad was born showing none of it. gravity_magnitude is a supporting export, not an axis - it is only ever read to DRAW the prediction, never applied to anybody.
dna.declines: forward_force / up_force / cooldown_time stay plain numeric exports - a bigger arrow is a size change, not a different claim

force_pad.name: Force Pad
force_pad.description: 1x1 m glowing launch pad. An Area3D on the player_body layer fires on contact, setting the player CharacterBody3D's velocity to forward+up. Pulsing surface, forward chevrons, live launch-vector arrow. DNA: forward_force (6), up_force (7), cooldown_time.
force_pad.qfep_connection: F_force: a velocity handed to the body (up + forward); gravity returns it to ground.

euler_drift.description: The forces seam. Continuous dynamics integrated in jumps: the true parabola (amber) vs the Euler path (blue) drifting off it, gaining energy it was never given; and at a big step a fast body tunnels clean through the wall. The force is real; the stepping is the machine's.
euler_drift.name: Euler Drift
euler_drift.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for forces. Bias is conserved; show the seam.
